title: Cab ride with Louis: learning 'Black and Blue'; offering him the tea
summary: Going to Harlem to see Willie the Lion, Louis teaches him 'Black and Blue' and McPartland offers him Mezzrow's box of pot.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: So what happened was we were in New York one time and Louis was in Hot Chocolates.
Yes, I've got many, many things from Hot Chocolates here in my files.

Yes, so I made a date with Louis one night. I was working also and after the show, and after his show we were going to get together and I'd finished at the Park Central Hotel there with Benny Pollack and his orchestra. And Milton Mezzrow had left me a whole cigar box full of tea. You know, we called it tea. If you want to call it, it's marijuana, pot. And I didn't want it because I wasn't smoking very much in those days. I used to whiff a little on scotch and stuff.
But I met Louis after the show had just opened
and we were going to go up in Harlem and sit in with Willie Lion the Lion. Willie Smith.
Willie Smith was Willie the Lion.

That's right. And so we made this date and on the way back, on the way up we were taking a cab just Louis and myself and I was telling Louis, I said ...... Oh, and first of all Louis was telling me about a song in the show, he says it was a killer, this is a killer McPartland. He used to call me McPartland, McPartland. He says it's a great number in the show he says called 'Black and Blue' you know. And I said, yes, how does it go? So he sang it to me. (SINGS). "old empty bed, springs hard as lead, wish I was dead, feel like old Ned, what did I do to be so black and blue.

So I loved the song and we'd sing in harmony you know. (SINGS).......... He's singing higher to me and I could hear the harmony. So he taught me the song on the way up, on the way up to see Willie the Lion Smith, at Rod and Jerry's up in Harlem you know.
So he happened to mention to me you know, hey McPartland, got any good tea around? I said, Milton Mezzrow left me a whole cigar box full of pot you know,
